chosen.title: Conversations That Never Happened: How Your Therapy Became Training Data
chosen.rationale: Virtual-therapy giants (Talkspace citing 153M patient messages) are racing to train chatbots on real therapy transcripts while rivals fabricate synthetic sessions, with 'consent' buried in terms and conditions — a data-colonialism story about the most intimate data there is, exactly Dawn's consent-labor-and-power register.

rejected_candidates.title: The Preemption Machine: Washington's Campaign to Erase Every State AI Law at Once
rejected_candidates.rationale: With Congress's moratorium struck down 99-1 but a December 2025 executive order now siccing the DOJ on state AI statutes — and Colorado already gutting its own landmark law under industry pressure — the fight over WHO gets to regulate AI is peaking in 2026; a follow-the-money federalism piece squarely in Dawn's corporate-capture-of-public-institutions beat (distinct from the earlier single-brief DOJ story).

sources.name: Ropes & Gray — federal push to override state AI regulation
Center for American Progress — preemption risks

rejected_candidates.title: Trust Nurses, Not AI: Algorithmic Management Comes for the People Who Keep You Alive
rejected_candidates.rationale: Kaiser call-center nurses — 25,000 now in CNA contract talks where AI is the flashpoint — say surveillance tools grading their 'empathy' and capping call times override professional judgment and threaten patient safety; a fresh labor-and-care angle on automation's human cost that goes beyond the generic keystroke-surveillance framing.
